intro: Where the quant track can lead: the main trading and quant jobs, and the rounds most firms put candidates through. Each one lists the units in this app that prepare you for it.

roles.title: Quant trader
roles.where: Prop trading firms, market makers, hedge funds and bank trading desks
roles.what: Runs trading strategies or quotes prices, deciding how much to trade and how much risk to hold, often within seconds. Many firms hire graduates straight from campus and teach the markets on the job.

roles.title: Quant researcher
roles.where: Hedge funds, prop trading firms and quant fund managers
roles.what: Looks for patterns in market data that predict prices, tests them hard and turns the ones that survive into strategies. It needs strong statistics and coding, and many hires have a master's or a PhD.

roles.title: Quant developer
roles.where: Trading firms, exchanges and brokers' technology teams
roles.what: Builds the systems that trade: market data feeds, order gateways, risk checks and backtesting tools. At high-frequency firms, shaving microseconds off the code is the job.
skills: How exchanges and order books work

roles.title: Execution trader
roles.where: Mutual funds, insurers, foreign funds and brokers' algo desks
roles.what: Buys and sells large orders for a fund without moving the price too much, choosing the algo, the venue and the timing, then measuring what it cost.
skills: Working with brokers and fund managers

roles.title: Risk manager
roles.where: Banks, brokers, clearing corporations, exchanges and funds
roles.what: Measures how much a desk or fund could lose and sets the limits, margins and stress tests that stop one bad day from sinking the firm.

roles.title: Rates and currency trader
roles.where: Bank treasuries, primary dealers and foreign banks
roles.what: Trades government bonds, T-bills, interest rate swaps and the rupee, reacting to RBI policy, inflation data and money flowing in and out of India.
skills: Bond maths: yield, duration and PV01

rounds.name: Online test
rounds.what: A timed test, often 30 to 60 minutes, of arithmetic, probability and number puzzles, sometimes with coding. Speed counts as much as accuracy.

rounds.name: Mental maths
rounds.what: Multiplying, dividing and working out percentages in your head, fast. Some firms run a set of quick-fire sums against a tight clock.

rounds.name: Probability and puzzles
rounds.what: Dice, cards, coins and brainteasers, worked out loud. Interviewers want to hear how you reason, so talk through each step and check your answer. Some also ask for a rough estimate of a size or a count.

rounds.name: Market-making game
rounds.what: The interviewer asks for a bid and an ask on something uncertain, like the total of some dice, trades with you and drops clues. You must move your prices and manage your position.

rounds.name: Markets and options
rounds.what: Why options cost what they do, the Greeks, put-call parity, futures fair value, and what's moving the market this week.

rounds.name: Statistics and research
rounds.what: Mostly for research roles: regression, overfitting, what can go wrong in a backtest, and a deep dive into a project of yours.

rounds.name: Coding
rounds.what: For research and developer roles: data structures, algorithms and handling data in Python or C++. This app doesn't teach coding, so practise it separately.

rounds.name: Fit and motivation
rounds.what: Why trading, how you handle a losing streak, and a project you're proud of. It's short, but it counts.

note: Every firm runs its own process, and it changes from year to year; this is the usual shape. Check each firm's careers page before you apply.
